title: Intent Rhythm: two-week sprint scratch and KPI sketch
body:
Purpose / context:
This is a personal scratchpad for the next two-week rhythm. Not a polished doc — thinking out loud about how to move 3 focus KPIs forward without burning out. Use this to capture mini-experiments, quick retros, and questions for 1:1s.

High-level objective (fortnight):
- Reduce context-switch friction and increase measurable deep-focus output for shipping product work and improving my onboarding docs.

Priority KPIs (tracked weekly):
- Deep Focus Hours (DFH): target 12 hours/week (baseline: 6-8)
- PR throughput: target 4 merged PRs / sprint (baseline: 1-2)
- Docs adoption: 5 unique internal views / week to my new onboarding doc + 2 comments/suggestions (baseline: 0)

Hypotheses to test:
1) Blocking off 90-min morning focus blocks will double DFH without decreasing reactive work SLA. (Measure: calendar blocked vs actual DFH logged)
2) Bundling small doc edits into a single review pass reduces PR latency and increases merged PRs. (Measure: PR age and # of review rounds)
3) Quick micro-demos (5m) at team async channel will increase doc views and feedback.

Mini experiment plan (week 1):
- Monday: Block 2 x 90-min focus blocks (9:00–10:30, 14:00–15:30). Tag calendar "DFH".
- Tuesday: Triage inbox only 2x (11:30, 16:00). Keep Slack DND during DFH.
- Wednesday: Batch doc edits for onboarding guide; open PR before EOD.
- Thursday: Micro-demo post (screenshot + 2-line summary) in #eng-ops.
- Friday: Retro + metric check: measure DFH, PRs, doc views.

Measurement notes / simple log (manual; quick numbers):
- 2026-03-02 (Tue): DFH = 3.0h (blocked 2 x 90min but only 1 block fully uninterrupted). Email spikes from 11:30 triage bled into afternoon.
- 2026-03-03 (Wed): DFH = 2.5h. Opened onboarding-doc PR (#42).
- 2026-03-04 (Thu): DFH = 1.5h. Posted micro-demo in #eng-ops (see linked_artifacts). Doc got 3 views, 1 comment (promising).
- 2026-03-05 (Fri): DFH = 2.0h. PR still waiting on review (requested from Marcus).
- Week 1 total DFH = 9.0h (short of 12h goal). PRs merged: 0. Doc views: 3.

Initial retro (end of week 1):
- Wins: Micro-demo drove at least one actionable comment. Blocking calendar helped preserve some focused time.
- Frictions: Slack/email interruptions still highest failure mode — triage windows shifted unexpectedly. PR bottleneck is review latency (Marcus busy).
- Quick fixes: Move one DFH to earlier (8:30 start) to avoid midday traffic. Ping reviewers with a short checklist in PR description to lower review friction.

Adjustments for week 2:
- Start first DFH at 8:30. Shorten second DFH to 60 min and put a 10-min buffer to process urgent items.
- Add "PR reviewer checklist" snippet to PR description: purpose, quick files changed, test steps, estimate review time (5-10m).
- Schedule a 10-min sync with Marcus to unblock PR path (if he cannot, look for alternate reviewer).
- Post micro-demo on Thursday and explicitly ask 2 people for feedback.

Week 2 quick log (ongoing):
- 2026-03-08 (Mon): DFH = 3.5h (8:30 start worked). Merged small infra config PR.
- 2026-03-09 (Tue): DFH = 2.0h. PR #42 got first review from Marcus; left small comments.
- 2026-03-10 (Wed): DFH = 3.0h. Addressed comments, added unit test, pushed update.
- 2026-03-11 (Thu): DFH = 1.0h. Micro-demo posted, doc views up to 11 total, 3 comments.
- 2026-03-12 (Fri): DFH = 1.5h. PR #42 merged after quick follow-up.
- Week 2 total DFH = 11.0h. PRs merged: 2. Docs views: net +8.

Two-week summary (2026-03-01 to 2026-03-12):
- DFH total: 20.0h (~10h/week average; improvement but still below 12h target).
- PR merged: 2 (improved).
- Docs adoption: onboarding doc views increased; initial feedback loop established.

Learnings / notes:
- Morning earlier start captures higher uninterrupted time. Avoid scheduling reactive meetings before 11:00.
- Explicit reviewer checklist materially reduced context for reviewers and sped up merges.
- Micro-demos are low-friction, high-leverage for visibility; continue weekly.

Open questions / 1:1 agenda items:
- Can manager nudge reviewer capacity for quick PRs during sprints? (impact: unblock pipeline)
- Is there team appetite to adopt weekly 5-min micro-demo slot in async updates?
- Headcount ask angle: if we show steady PR throughput lift, can we justify a part-time tech writer for onboarding docs?

Next actions (immediately):
- Iterate PR checklist into a snippet template in my local PR template. (target: EOD next Tue)
- Schedule 10-min sync with Marcus or alternate reviewer. (target: next Mon)
- Draft short async post template for micro-demo (title, 1-sentence why, 2 bullet steps to try).

Backlog ideas (nice-to-have experiments):
- Track distraction sources in simple tag log (Slack vs email vs meetings) to quantify biggest leakage.
- Run 1-week email-batching-only challenge and compare DFH.
- Try a "pomodoro-light" cadence (4 x 25min) to see if more frequent resets help for shallow multitask days.

Quick links to artifacts mentioned:
- PR: internal-notes/pull/42 -> "onboarding doc PR" (linked above).
- Ticket: ENG-2768 (tech debt + docs follow-up).
- Confluence: Personal OKR playbook (notes + templates).

Misc (notes to self):
- Keep this doc short — move polished metrics to a small sheet if I want history visualization.
- Re-check measurement approach: consider simple Google Sheet with date / DFH / PRs / doc views for month view.

Status: continuing; will re-evaluate after next two-week window.

-- end of scratchpad entry (Chiara)
